_about: Single source for the lab's libraries and default comparisons. The page (LIBS, RUNTIME), the toolkit (build.mjs) and AUTHORING.md section 6 are generated from it. {{CDN}} is the package CDN base; {{THREE_HEAD}} and {{STORY3D_KIT}} are filled in by the host. "trios" is the bake-off skill's default contender table (docs/SKILL.lesson-visual-bakeoff.md section 2).

libraries.name: p5.js
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}p5@1.9.4/lib/p5.min.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tag loads p5 1.9.4 from jsDelivr before the code; global p5 exists; code must use instance mode inside root.
libraries.notes: p5.js 1.9.4 is loaded as the global constructor p5. Use INSTANCE mode only: inst = new p5(s => { s.setup = ...; s.draw = ...; }, root). Size the canvas to root.clientWidth x root.clientHeight, resize in s.windowResized, and call inst.remove() in destroy().

libraries.name: three.js
libraries.global: ES module: import * as THREE from 'three' (window.THREE also set)
libraries.head: <script type="importmap">{"imports":{"three":"{{CDN}}three@0.186.1/build/three.module.js","three/addons/":"{{CDN}}three@0.186.1/examples/jsm/"}}</script><script type="module">import * as T from 'three';import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';window.THREE=Object.assign({},T,{OrbitControls});window.OrbitControls=OrbitControls;</script>
libraries.runtime: an import map maps 'three' and 'three/addons/' to three r186 on jsDelivr; a prelude module then sets window.THREE (with THREE.OrbitControls) and window.OrbitControls; the code runs as the next module. So 'THREE is not defined' can only mean the library failed to load (look for 'Failed to load' in Problems) or the code ran outside the module order.
libraries.notes: three.js r186. The code runs as an ES module after an import map: prefer import * as THREE from 'three'; import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'. A prelude module also defines window.THREE (including THREE.OrbitControls) and window.OrbitControls before your code runs. Append renderer.domElement to root, size it to root, cap pixel ratio at 2, use renderer.setAnimationLoop, handle resize with a ResizeObserver on root. Put text in an absolutely positioned HTML overlay div inside root. destroy() stops the loop, disposes controls, geometries, materials and the renderer, and empties root.

libraries.name: Chart.js
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}chart.js@4.6.1/dist/chart.umd.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tag loads Chart.js 4.6.1 UMD; global Chart exists before the code.
libraries.notes: Chart.js 4.6.1 is loaded as the global Chart. Create a wrapper div (width/height 100%) with a canvas inside root; set responsive: true and maintainAspectRatio: false. update() changes chart.data / options and calls chart.update(); destroy() calls chart.destroy().

libraries.name: Plotly.js
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}plotly.js-dist-min@2.35.2/plotly.min.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tag loads plotly.js-dist-min 2.35.2; global Plotly exists before the code.
libraries.notes: Plotly.js 2.35.2 is loaded as the global Plotly. Plot into a div filling root with Plotly.newPlot(div, data, layout, {responsive: true, displaylogo: false}). update() uses Plotly.react; destroy() calls Plotly.purge(div). No MathJax, no remote fonts or map tiles.

libraries.name: D3
libraries.purpose: custom data visualization: scales, axes, data joins and full control over every mark
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}d3@7.9.0/dist/d3.min.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tag loads d3 7.9.0 UMD from jsDelivr; global d3 exists before the code.
libraries.notes: D3 7.9.0 is loaded as the global d3 (no d3-cloud plugin here; use the wordcloud library for word clouds). Build one <svg> in root with d3.select(root).append('svg') sized to root; use d3 scales (scaleLinear, scaleBand, scaleTime), d3.axisBottom/axisLeft, data joins with selection.join(), and label marks directly. update() redraws from model(params). For seek(t), compute and draw the exact state at t; do not rely on running d3 transitions for lesson progress. destroy() removes the svg and any listeners.

libraries.name: Word cloud (D3 + d3-cloud)
libraries.purpose: a word cloud of terms sized by importance and coloured by theme, D3 + d3-cloud
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}d3@7.9.0/dist/d3.min.js"></script><script src="{{CDN}}d3-cloud@1.2.9/build/d3.layout.cloud.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tags load d3 7.9.0 and then d3-cloud 1.2.9 from jsDelivr; d3.layout.cloud exists before the code.
libraries.notes: D3 7.9.0 (global d3) plus d3-cloud 1.2.9, which adds d3.layout.cloud(). Lay out once in mount(), update() and on resize, never in seek(): d3.layout.cloud().size([w, h]).words(terms.map(t => ({ text: t.text, src: t }))).padding(3).rotate(0).font(FONT).fontWeight(600).fontSize(d => scale(d.src.weight)).random(seededRandom).timeInterval(Infinity).on('end', words => { placed = words; }).start(). With timeInterval(Infinity) the 'end' event fires synchronously. d3-cloud overwrites the text, weight, size and position fields on each word object, so keep your data in d.src. Words that do not fit are dropped: compare placed.length with the input, retry with a smaller font scale, and say on screen if any are missing. Use a seeded random function (for example mulberry32) so the cloud does not reshuffle on every update. Draw with an svg <text text-anchor=middle> per placed word at translate(w/2 + d.x, h/2 + d.y) with font-size d.size. Keep rotate(0) so every word reads horizontally. seek(t) only changes opacity or colour, for example revealing words in rank order.

libraries.name: Sankey (D3 + d3-sankey)
libraries.purpose: flows that split and merge between stages, band width = amount: funnels, budgets, records, tokens or money moving between systems, D3 + d3-sankey
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}d3@7.9.0/dist/d3.min.js"></script><script src="{{CDN}}d3-sankey@0.12.3/dist/d3-sankey.min.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tags load d3 7.9.0 and then d3-sankey 0.12.3 from jsDelivr; d3.sankey and d3.sankeyLinkHorizontal exist before the code.
libraries.notes: D3 7.9.0 (global d3) plus d3-sankey 0.12.3, whose UMD build adds d3.sankey(), d3.sankeyLinkHorizontal() and the aligns (d3.sankeyJustify, sankeyLeft, sankeyRight, sankeyCenter) to the global d3. Lay out in mount(), update() and on resize, never in seek(): G = d3.sankey().nodeId(d => d.id).nodeWidth(14).nodePadding(20).nodeSort(null).extent([[12, top], [w - 12, h - 12]])({ nodes: model.nodes.map(n => ({ ...n })), links: model.links.map(l => ({ ...l })) }). d3-sankey mutates what you pass: it replaces link.source/target ids with node objects and adds x0, x1, y0, y1, value, depth, layer and width, so always hand it fresh copies. nodeId(d => d.id) lets links name nodes by id instead of array index. nodeSort(null) keeps the model's order in every column; without it nodes are re-sorted by position and bands swap places when a slider moves. The default align (justify) moves every end node to the last column, so read columns from node.layer, not node.depth. Leave out zero-value links and nodes before layout, otherwise they still take a slot and padding, and say on screen what was dropped ("0 records"). Draw each link as a path with d = d3.sankeyLinkHorizontal(), fill none, stroke-width max(1, d.width), coloured by target, and each node as a rect; put labels right of the node in the left half and left of it in the right half, with a white halo (paint-order stroke) and the value in the label. Keep the node count under about 20 and labels short so a phone frame can hold it; at narrow widths drop the value from the labels. seek(t) only reveals and never relayouts: draw bands in stage by stage with stroke-dasharray = path length and stroke-dashoffset, fade nodes in as their bands arrive, or move particles along the link paths. Watch root with a ResizeObserver rather than the window resize event: the host adds rows after mount, which shrinks root. Do not name a top-level const top (it collides with window.top).

libraries.name: React Flow
libraries.purpose: interactive process, workflow and architecture diagrams
libraries.runtime: React 18.3.1 UMD, ReactDOM UMD, a jsx-runtime shim and @xyflow/react 12.12.0 UMD load first; globals React, ReactDOM, ReactFlow exist; no JSX compiler.
libraries.notes: React 18.3.1 (globals React, ReactDOM) and React Flow 12 (global namespace ReactFlow: ReactFlow.ReactFlow, ReactFlow.Background, ReactFlow.Controls, ReactFlow.MarkerType, ReactFlow.Position, ReactFlow.Handle). There is NO JSX compiler: use const h = React.createElement. Render with const r = ReactDOM.createRoot(root); give the ReactFlow element style {width:'100%', height:'100%'} and fitView. update() re-renders with new params; destroy() calls r.unmount(). The React Flow stylesheet is already loaded. fitView never zooms out past minZoom (0.5 by default), so a wide diagram is clipped on a phone: set minZoom: 0.2, and call fitView again after a resize.

libraries.name: Cytoscape.js
libraries.purpose: network graphs laid out automatically (routing, dependencies, social graphs), with algorithm state drawn on nodes and edges
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}cytoscape@3.34.4/dist/cytoscape.min.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tag loads Cytoscape.js 3.34.4 from jsDelivr; global cytoscape exists before the code.
libraries.notes: Cytoscape.js 3.34.4 is loaded as the global cytoscape. It draws nodes, edges and their labels on a canvas, so put the values the learner must read in an HTML caption too. Create once in mount(): cy = cytoscape({container, elements, style, autoungrabify: true, autounselectify: true, userZoomingEnabled: false, userPanningEnabled: false, boxSelectionEnabled: false}), with the container a sized div filling root. Style with a stylesheet array of {selector, style} (node, edge, node.settled, edge.route...) and hex palette literals; label: 'data(label)' with text-wrap: 'wrap' for two-line labels, and text-background-color/-opacity so edge labels stay readable over lines. Use built-in layouts only (no extensions are loaded): breadthfirst with roots and directed: false puts one row per hop from the root, which suits search and shortest-path lessons; circle, concentric and grid are also stable; cose is random unless randomize: false. Every layout spreads nodes over the container's size at the moment it runs, so pass a fixed boundingBox ({x1: 0, y1: 0, w: 780, h: 460}) to get the same layout at every size, then cy.fit(undefined, 24). For hand-placed graphs, use layout 'preset' with positions from the model. Run the layout in mount(), and in update() only if the set of nodes or edges changed; a removed or failed link is a class (dashed line), not a re-layout, so nothing jumps. seek(t) restyles with cy.batch(() => { n.data('label', ...); n.toggleClass('settled', ...); }) and never runs a layout. Labels of two crossing edges overlap at their midpoints: slide each along its edge with text-margin-x/-y from data. ResizeObserver on the container calls cy.resize() and cy.fit(). destroy() disconnects the observer and calls cy.destroy(). See examples/routes_cytoscape.js.

libraries.name: Mermaid
libraries.purpose: sequence diagrams of messages between people and systems (auth handshakes, API calls, events), stepped one message at a time
libraries.head: <script src="{{CDN}}mermaid@12.2.0/dist/mermaid.min.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tag loads the Mermaid 12.2.0 single-file browser build (about 5.5 MB) from jsDelivr; global mermaid exists before the code; mermaid.render is async.
libraries.notes: Mermaid 12.2.0 is loaded as the global mermaid. Call mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: 'strict', theme: 'base', themeVariables: {...}, sequence: {mirrorActors: false, showSequenceNumbers: true, useMaxWidth: false}}) once. Build the diagram text from model(params): 'sequenceDiagram', one 'participant ID as Label' (or 'actor') line per participant, then one 'FROM->>TO: text' line per step ('-->>' for a reply, '-x' or '--x' for a rejected call). Strip ';' and '#' from message text: Mermaid reads them as a line break and an entity. mermaid.render(uniqueId, text) returns a Promise of {svg}: use a new id per render, ignore results from stale renders, and push failures to window.__errors. Put the svg in a div filling root; remove its inline style and set width and height 100% with preserveAspectRatio 'xMidYMin meet'. Each message renders as text.messageText, then its arrow (.messageLine0 solid, .messageLine1 dotted), then text.sequenceNumber, in step order, so index i of each list is step i. seek(t) stores t and restyles those elements (dim future steps, highlight the current one); it must also work before the first render resolves, so draw from the stored t once the svg arrives. Re-render on update() and only when the width crosses a narrow breakpoint (shorter participant labels below about 640 px), not on every resize. Put the current step's sentence in an HTML caption under the diagram. destroy() disconnects observers, invalidates pending renders and empties root.

libraries.name: Story (SVG + GSAP + icons)
libraries.purpose: animated explainer with people, agents, code windows, documents and scores, built from SVG, GSAP and icons; best for pipelines and processes told as a story
libraries.runtime: classic <script> tags load GSAP 3.15 (global gsap) and Lucide 1.61 (global lucide) from jsDelivr, then a helper defines labIcon(name, attrs) that returns an SVG icon element; no external images are allowed, so pictures must be icons or SVG shapes.
libraries.notes: An animated explainer drawn in one SVG. GSAP 3.15 (global gsap) and Lucide 1.61 icons are loaded. labIcon(name, attrs) returns an <svg> icon element for a kebab-case Lucide name, for example 'user', 'users', 'bot', 'code', 'test-tube', 'search', 'bug', 'package', 'server', 'lock', 'shield-check', 'gauge', 'database', 'file-text', 'git-branch', 'refresh-cw', 'user-check', 'ticket', 'brain', 'wrench'; attrs such as {x, y, width, height, stroke}; append it inside your SVG. Build one <svg viewBox='0 0 1000 545' width='100%' height='100%'> in root. Draw people, agents, devices, code windows, documents and scores with icons and SVG shapes; no external images. Build ONE paused gsap.timeline() from model data: one scene group per step, shown with tl.set(group, {opacity: 1}, start) and hidden at its end, with tweens inside each scene. The duration getter returns the model's total; seek(t) calls tl.seek(t, false) and also sets step titles and highlight states directly from the current step, because tl.call callbacks do not reverse when scrubbing back. Set initial states with gsap.set before adding tweens. update() kills the timeline and rebuilds it. Use the palette hex values from the look rules exactly (ink #1d2433, muted #5b6475, line #dbe0e8, accent #2b59c3, highlight #c2410c, good #1f7a4d, #0f766e, #b4530f, white cards, light tints): the viewer's Look (Night sky, Studio, Blueprint) re-colours those literals at display time, so other colours will not follow the look.

libraries.name: 3D story (three.js)
libraries.purpose: the same kind of story as a three.js scene with a camera that travels between steps; use when a spatial journey helps, otherwise prefer story
libraries.head: {{THREE_HEAD}}<script src="{{CDN}}lucide@1.61.0/dist/umd/lucide.min.js"></script><script type="module">{{STORY3D_KIT}}</script><script src="{{CDN}}gsap@3.15.0/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
libraries.runtime: an import map plus prelude module provide three r186 (window.THREE with OrbitControls), then a module defines the global Story3D kit (Story3D.mount(root, config) returns {seek, update, destroy, duration, markers}; props: cards, robot, monitor, magnifier, servers, chain, shield, bars, gate, pages, database, people, rocket), and GSAP 3.15 loads as global gsap; the code runs as a module. Good 3D story code is a short config() adapter over the kit; hand-built scenes are the usual cause of flat, cluttered results.
libraries.notes: Build it with the Story3D kit, which is already loaded as the global Story3D (it brings three.js r186, props, camera flights, labels and exact seeking). Do not build your own three.js scene. Write a config(m) function that turns model(params) output into {title, summary, duration, stations, events, loops}. A station is {id, label, prop, icon?, values?, pages?, count?, locked?}; icon is an optional kebab-case Lucide icon name for the floating badge above the station (each prop has a sensible default). prop is one of: cards (tickets or items arrive), robot (an AI agent plans), monitor (a screen showing a title, typed code lines and a status sequence), magnifier (inspection that raises red flags or a green OK), servers (a package deploys to a target rack; a second rack is padlocked unless locked is false), chain (linked traceability), shield (governance; event mode observe or enforce), bars (scores from values 0-100, optional stacked pages), gate (approval gate with a person; event open true or false), pages (documents stack; count), database (a data store), people (a team; count), rocket (a launch). Pick the prop that best fits each step's meaning. An event is {station, start, dur, title, note, loop?, flags?, ok?, mode?, open?, screen?}, with start and dur in playback seconds, note one sentence under 110 characters, flags the number of red markers on a magnifier, ok true for a passing inspection, and screen {title, status: [{label, color}], typing, highlightLine} for a monitor. loops is [{from, to, label}] for rework arcs; set loop: true on events that travel them. Then: let story; window.lab = { get duration() { return story.duration; }, get markers() { return story.markers; }, seek(t) { story.seek(t); }, mount(root, p) { story = Story3D.mount(root, config(model(p))); }, update(p) { story.update(config(model(p))); }, destroy() { story.destroy(); } }. Colors, lighting and fonts come from the viewer's chosen look (Night sky, Studio or Blueprint), so never set colors or materials yourself.

libraries.name: Plain SVG
libraries.purpose: plain SVG, no library, hand-built for full flexibility
libraries.runtime: no library; plain DOM and SVG APIs.
libraries.notes: No library. Build an <svg> with document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', ...) sized to root, use requestAnimationFrame for animation and cancel it in destroy().

comparisons.when: vocabulary, key terms, buzzwords or jargon
comparisons.learn: Visual impact versus accurate comparison: can learners tell which term matters most?
comparisons.formA: a word cloud: size shows weight, colour shows theme, every word horizontal
comparisons.formB: a ranked horizontal bar chart of the same terms, largest at the top, coloured by theme

comparisons.when: auth handshakes, API calls, webhooks or events passed between people and systems in order
comparisons.learn: Precise notation versus a narrated story: can learners say who sent what to whom, and in what order?
comparisons.formA: a UML sequence diagram, one message lit per step
comparisons.formB: an animated story of the same messages travelling between the same participants

comparisons.when: an amount splits and merges across stages and nothing is created or lost
comparisons.learn: Flow versus totals: stacked bars give exact stage totals, but only the Sankey shows which part went where.
comparisons.formA: a Sankey: band width shows the amount, traced from source to outcome
comparisons.formB: one stacked bar per stage, each adding up to the same total

comparisons.when: shortest paths, search order, dependency or routing graphs
comparisons.learn: Automatic layout versus a hand-placed map: does arranging nodes by hop count make the algorithm's choice easier to see than placing them where they are?

trios.concept: Protocol, handshake, API calls, messages between systems

alt.as: sequence diagram, one message lit per step
the same messages as an animated story
who talks to whom, without the order
custom data graphic: own scales, axes and marks, annotations where they matter

trios.concept: Flows and volumes: funnels, budgets, data moving between systems (where records, tokens or money go)

alt.as: Sankey trace: fastest to a readable flow
full control of labels, reveal order and particles
the same stages told as a journey
ranked bars: the honest version of the same data
